findings.title: Silence menu item can be shown but clicking it does nothing when only a Prometheus rule is provided
findings.body: GrafanaRuleListItem renders RuleActionsButtons with only promRule and no ruler rule. AlertRuleMenu can render the 'Silence notifications' item because canSilence is now also computed from the Grafana Prometheus rule abilities. Clicking that item sets showSilenceDrawer to true, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is only rendered when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. When rule is undefined, this condition is false, so the drawer is never rendered and the visible Silence action is a no-op.

findings.title: skipToken does not neutralize Grafana Prometheus rule abilities
findings.body: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities converts skipToken to undefined and calls useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities. That hook does not treat an undefined rule as absent: when loading is false it sets MaybeSupported to AlwaysSupported, so abilities such as Duplicate can become [true, true] based only on permissions. AlertRuleMenu ORs these Grafana abilities with ruler abilities, which can incorrectly enable Duplicate for non-Grafana rules, missing rules, or rules that should be unsupported. A skip token should result in [false, false] for all requested actions.

findings.title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body: useAllRulerRuleAbilities hard-codes isFederated = false, and the deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to it. Previously useAllAlertRuleAbilities used isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) to make federated rules immutable. After this change, federated Mimir rules may be considered editable, deletable, pausable, or restorable, exposing actions that should be disabled and risking modification of rules that are intended to be read-only.

findings.title: Missing React key for GrafanaRuleListItem in filtered rule list
findings.body: In FilterViewResults, the datasource and unknown rule branches pass key={key}, but the Grafana branch returns GrafanaRuleListItem without a key. React will emit missing-key warnings and may reuse list-item state incorrectly when the list changes. The available key variable should be passed to GrafanaRuleListItem.

findings.title: Menu test verifies Silence item exists but does not exercise it
findings.body: The test asserts that the Silence notifications menu item is rendered, but it never clicks the item or asserts that a silence drawer opens. This misses the current bug where the Silence action is visible in the Prometheus-only list view but does nothing when clicked because no ruler rule is available.

findings.title: Extra closing brace in Grafana rule key
findings.body: getGrafanaRuleKey returns a template string ending with an extra `}`, producing keys like `grafana-<namespaceUid>-<groupName>-<ruleUid>}`. This is likely a typo and makes generated keys harder to debug; the trailing extra brace should be removed.

findings.title: Clipboard write promise rejection is unhandled
findings.body: copyToClipboard calls navigator.clipboard?.writeText(text).then(...) without a catch handler. If the clipboard write fails, the promise rejection is unhandled and the user receives no feedback. A rejection handler should be added, ideally with an error toast or fallback.

findings.title: Component comment still says ruler endpoint is used
findings.body: GrafanaGroupLoader's comment says it loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints, but the ruler query was removed in this PR. The component now only polls the Prometheus endpoint. The comment and the nearby expectedRulesCount comment referencing Ruler responses should be updated.

findings.title: Stale comment about preloading ruler rules
findings.body: After removing the alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup') call, the comment still says this step preloads ruler rules and improves UX by avoiding waiting for each group to load. The remaining code only upserts Prometheus query data, so the comment is misleading.
